An English crib of the Latin text, semi-literal, made for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model (LLM) made by Anthropic. It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: ECf retr 5.3a
div.ab: Et si forte redierit, nullus eum hospitari presumat, nisi a rege data licentia.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 631 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page; the words in bold are the Retractator’s changes to ECf, as Liebermann prints them.

div.ab: And if perchance he returns, let no one presume to harbour him, except by licence given by the king.
